# Summary of the Political Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a programme for national renewal, addressing economic recovery, public service reform, and political accountability following two major crises: a global financial downturn and a parliamentary expenses scandal.

## Economic Recovery and Growth

The manifesto prioritises securing economic recovery by maintaining current public spending levels before transitioning to deficit reduction—aiming to halve the deficit within four years through growth, fair taxation, and targeted spending cuts. The banking system would be reformed through stricter regulation, capital requirements, and a global levy on financial services. A new finance initiative would bring together £4 billion to support growing businesses, with investment focused on high-tech industries, green energy, and infrastructure including high-speed rail and universal broadband access.

## Employment and Welfare

The plan guarantees jobs or training for young people unemployed for six months, with mandatory participation after ten months. Those unemployed for two years would receive guaranteed work placements. The National Minimum Wage would rise at least with average earnings, and a "Better Off in Work" guarantee would ensure families are at least £40 weekly better off working than on benefits. Advanced apprenticeships would be expanded, and skills accounts would help workers upgrade their qualifications.

## Public Services

Healthcare would see legally binding guarantees including cancer test results within one week and maximum 18-week treatment waits. Preventative care would expand through routine check-ups for over-40s. Frontline education spending would increase, with guaranteed tutoring for children falling behind and expansion of free nursery places. Police and community support officer numbers would be maintained, with neighbourhood teams spending 80% of their time visible in local areas.

## Social Support

Measures include a new "Father's Month" of flexible paid leave, a Toddler Tax Credit of £4 weekly, and flexible working rights for older workers alongside ending default retirement at 65. A National Care Service would provide free home care for those with greatest needs and cap residential care costs after two years.

## Political Reform

The manifesto proposes referenda on electoral reform and House of Lords changes, fixed-term parliaments, a statutory register of lobbyists, and a commission on developing a written constitution. Local government would receive strengthened powers over public services.
